overall: The AG found the Nantucket Energy Study Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside a meeting on a video and by allowing remote participation before adoption; the notice timing complaint failed, though the AG said topics should have been more specific.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum of the Committee deliberated outside a posted meeting to create and broadcast a YouTube video on a Town Meeting warrant article.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore we find  that the Committee deliberated outside of a meeting to develop or decide to appear in the video.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the Committee's April 5, 2012 meeting was not posted at least 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide notice for its April 5, 2012 meeting.

allegations.summary: Notice filed in January listed the same six boilerplate topics for 11 meetings; the AG reviewed whether topics were specific enough for the April 5 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Although its notice was timely posted, the Committee should have provided a more detailed notice closer to the April 5, 2012 meeting date and included a detailed list of the topics "the chair reasonably anticipates will be discussed at the meeting."

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a Committee member was allowed to participate remotely at the April 5, 2012 meeting although the Town had not adopted remote participation under 940 CMR 29.10.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, members of Nantucket public bodies were not permitted to participate in meetings remotely, and the Committee violated the law when a member participated in the April 5, 2012 meeting remotely.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance the Open Meeting Law, and caution that a future similar violation may be considered an intentional violation of the law.

Committee members must attend a training on the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18­25, within sixty (60) days of reconstitution, to be conducted by an attorney or organization familiar with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law and approved by this office.
